clue.text: Devotion, if returned, left in god's keeping

indicators.note: returned means the little word if is sent back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: taken as written before turning

indicators.note: keeping means the god holds the next piece safely within it

parts.note: a god is a deity

explanation.surface: Someone's devotion, if given back, is left in the care of a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives FI; 'keeping' has the god holding L, making DELITY. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness and loyalty are the core senses of devotion, synonyms of the answer.

clue.text: Compact sort of biscuit

definitions.meaning: a flat case holding face powder and a mirror
a chewy oat bar or flat cake

explanation.surface: A dense type of biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat ladies' powder case and a baked oat-and-syrup bar.

clue.text: Image maker can exploit natural strengths

definitions.meaning: the chemical that brings out the picture on photographic film
a builder who exploits land and its resources

explanation.surface: A photographer can exploit natural talents.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic chemical brings out pictures, and a property builder exploits land's potential.

clue.text: Sticky sweet

parts.note: read as stick-y, a sweet mounted on a stick, not a gooey one

explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick, a lollipop, is a sweet on a stick in the literal sense.

clue.text: In a way, I used to find it boring

indicators.note: in a way means shaken into another way of ordering, signalling the letters of I used to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they once found something dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' rearranges IUSEDTO; 'find it' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and wearisome things are described this way; a synonym.

clue.text: Put the plate back, beast

indicators.note: put back here means the word for plate is set down in reverse order

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a plate to its place, then a cry of 'beast'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAMINA, a thin plate, into the answer; 'Put the' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature of the non-human kind, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Standard of rightness in nonconforming Pennine church

indicators.note: nonconforming means not keeping to the usual order, so the letters of Pennine are rearranged

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A nonconformist chapel in the Pennines as a model of correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonconforming' rearranges PENNINE into NINEPEN. 'Right as ninepence' is a British phrase for perfectly well; ninepence was an old coin sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as right as ninepence' makes this sum a byword for being in good order.

clue.text: Relatives in the stone business

parts.note: ma, a mother, is a relative
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A family firm of stone-cutters.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who cuts and lays stone works in that trade, a builder in stone.

clue.text: Layabout lifted lots — nothing missing in the end

annotationWithheld.why: Layabout lifted lots - nothing missing in the end (6): the parse needs LAY around rev(LOTS less O), so the single printed word 'Layabout' gives LAY and also 'about' as the container indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Layabout lifted lots — nothing missing in the end

clue.text: Keep the peace, so to speak

definitions.meaning: a keep is a fortified tower or stronghold
said aloud, peace is piece: a chessman

explanation.surface: Maintain law and order, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep the peace' reads as one phrase; split it: the keep is a fort, and 'peace, so to speak' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a keep, and the rook in chess is one of the pieces.

clue.text: A lot from Roman villa comes under the hammer

definitions.note: describes the thing that sits beneath a smith's hammer; a noun phrase in sense, the block struck on

indicators.note: a lot from means a portion is taken out of the following words, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An item from a Roman villa is put up for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the hammer' suggests an auction, with 'lot' to match; in fact it is the smith's block, lying across romAN VILla.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith lays hot metal on this iron block and strikes it, so it literally lies below the hammer.

clue.text: How do I assign changes in problem identification?

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of do I assign get rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about how a person should assign alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is only a link; 'changes' rearranges DOIASSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's or engineer's finding of what is wrong is exactly this kind of identifying of the fault.

clue.text: Tender and good-humoured about a duck is cricketer

parts.note: jolly means cheerful and good-humoured

indicators.note: about means the cricketer's word wraps around the duck and the a

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
a duck, a score of nothing in cricket, looks like O

explanation.surface: A gentle, cheerful cricketer is out for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places O and A inside BAT to give BOAT. A tender is a small boat serving a larger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's small boat that ferries people ashore is called a tender, and this is one such craft.

clue.text: Punishing with prison a notorious gangster

parts.note: pen is slang for a penitentiary, a prison
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A harsh sentence served in jail for an infamous mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws or measures inflicting punishment are described as such, as in a punitive code.

clue.text: Business good and plentiful

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
pious means devout, morally good

explanation.surface: A company that is both virtuous and wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant, plentiful supply is the meaning; a synonym.

clue.text: Look up plant, in a sense

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: relating to one of the five senses

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for look is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Examine a factory, in one meaning of the word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sense' sounds like a hedge; it is the definition, concerning the sense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the sense of smell, so it pertains to one of the senses.

clue.text: 'E topped and tailed quinces in a salad for a girl

parts.note: taken as written, the letter E

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture, so the letters are tossed into a fresh order
topped and tailed means the first and last letters of the fruit are cut off

explanation.surface: A cockney cook trims quinces and drops them into a salad for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' strips the first and last letters of quinces, leaving UINCE, which 'salad' tosses into UNICE after the dropped-H 'E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a woman's given name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: In describing weather, centigrade is decisive

indicators.note: in means the temperature letter is placed inside the weather word

parts.note: climatic means relating to climate, the weather
C is the abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: A forecast with centigrade readings proves crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts C inside CLIMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the decisive turning point, so this means forming a culmination.

clue.text: Worried and old, I get all knotted up inside

indicators.note: inside means the following pieces go within the word for old

parts.note: aged means old
to tat is to make lace by knotting thread

explanation.surface: An anxious old person is in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the pieces within the word for old. Tatting is lace made by knotting thread, hence 'get all knotted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious and flustered are synonyms, both describing a troubled state.

clue.text: Attack on good player's benefit

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the attack after the player

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is a good player
a fit is an attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: A strike against a skilled player turns to his advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gain or advantage is the sense; a synonym.

clue.text: Mavis embraced by Gareth Rushworth

definitions.note: an old name for the song thrush

indicators.note: embraced by means the word sits held within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A woman named Mavis is hugged by a man called Gareth Rushworth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mavis' looks like a woman's name; it is a country name for the song thrush, lying in gareTH RUSHworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is a dialect and poetic name for the song thrush, a bird.

clue.text: Attending to man with racket breaking for instance

parts.note: he refers to a man

indicators.note: breaking means the racket splits the example abbreviation apart

parts.note: e.g., for example
din means a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A man with a tennis racket breaks, perhaps, while listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts DIN between E and G to give EDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying attention to, minding and listening are what this verb means.

clue.text: Peaceful and holy — can alter

indicators.note: alter means change, so the letters of holy and can are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A calm, devout person can change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' rearranges HOLYCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are calm, untroubled ones; a synonym.

clue.text: A big old bird eats up live little creature

indicators.note: eats means the bird swallows the next piece, holding it within

parts.note: the moa was a huge extinct bird of New Zealand

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for live is read backwards

parts.note: be means to live, exist

explanation.surface: A large prehistoric bird gobbles up a tiny living thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for live into EB; 'eats' has the moa, a giant extinct New Zealand bird, swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism is a microscopic animal, a tiny creature.

clue.text: A score on the staff

parts.note: a score as in a written orchestral part, set out on the five lines of a ... stave, rather than twenty employees

explanation.definitionFit: Notes written on a staff (stave) form a score, which is written melody and harmony.

clue.text: Indian's cry cut short

definitions.note: read as 'Indian is': a North American Indian woman

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the cry is chopped off

parts.note: a squawk is a harsh cry

explanation.surface: An Indian's shout breaks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter from SQUAWK. The answer is an old, now offensive term for a Native American woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was used for a Native American woman, so she is a member of that people.

clue.text: Not willing to cut antler about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of cut antler are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone loath to trim a deer's antler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CUTANTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling and reluctant are synonyms, both describing hesitation.

clue.text: Many are fond of spice

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
love means to be fond of

explanation.surface: Lots of people like a particular seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried flower bud used to flavour food is a classic spice.

clue.text: Competing with bird in a bad way, I quit

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: quit means the letter I departs from the phrase it was in

parts.note: lousily means badly, in a poor way

explanation.surface: A rival to a bird is doing poorly, so the speaker gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quit' removes the I from LOUSILY, leaving LOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulous means eager to rival or outdo, so acting this way is vying or striving.

clue.text: Oarsmen, perhaps, and others going into reverse

indicators.note: reverse means the whole assembled sequence is read backwards at the end
going here means the others go inside the next word

parts.note: into can mean to, as in going to a place
etc, et cetera, means and others

explanation.surface: Rowers and others are backing water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' places et cetera inside the word for into, making TETCO, and 'reverse' turns the whole of it. A racing eight is a crew of eight rowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a group of eight people, a set of the kind this word names.

clue.text: Laws get tossed around for ever and ever

indicators.note: around means the shuffled laws wrap the next piece
get tossed means the letters of laws are thrown into another order

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word meaning ever

explanation.surface: Statutes are thrown about endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get tossed' rearranges the laws into ALWS; 'around' wraps them round AY, an old poetic word for ever, from the second 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally and perpetually express the meaning, synonyms of the answer.

clue.text: In France, one fought without paling

parts.note: un is French for one
fenced means fought with swords

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fought a duel without turning pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paling' looks like turning white with fear; here it means a fence of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A paling is a wooden fence, so land lacking one has no fence.
